Hack the Fork Paris
Track 3: protein sovereignty

SoyMate

A seed grade from a phone photo,
that the farmer can check too.

Federico Bello · Juan Pedro Maestrone · Pedro Pertusso

soymate.team@gmail.com

At harvest, someone at the cooperative spreads a sample from each truck on a table and counts the damaged seeds by eye. That count sets what the farmer is paid. SoyMate does it from one phone photo, and says how sure it is. (~10 s)

The problem

In 2025, a lot of French lentils were eaten by a beetle

1 seed in 4

had a beetle hole in an average truckload of French lentils, the worst year since the survey began in 2021

From 1 % to 75 %

some truckloads were almost clean, others had 3 seeds in 4 damaged

Bruchid: a small beetle. Its larva grows inside the seed and leaves a round hole when it comes out.

Source: Terres Univia / Terres Inovia, lentil seed quality survey, harvest 2025: mean 24.4 % damaged seeds per lot, 40 lots measured, range 1.0 to 75.5 %.

In 2025, French lentils had their worst bruchid year since the survey began in 2021: across 40 measured lots, an average of 24.4 % damaged seeds, from 1 % to 75 % between lots. No field spray against it is authorised any more. (~15 s)

The problem

Today, the damage is counted by hand, by eye

Counted by hand

When a truck arrives, someone spreads a few hundred seeds on a table and counts the bad ones.

Different people, different results

Two people, or two sites, can give the same truck a different grade, especially in the harvest rush.

The farmer can’t check

They learn the result when they deliver, with no photo or record to look at.

Sources: Codex standard CXS 171 (“visual examination”); LABOSEM 2022 (200-500 seeds); Farm Online 20/3/2025 (graders differ “from person to person”). Third card: our reading.

Today that damage is counted by eye on a few hundred seeds. Two people or two sites can give the same truck a different grade, and the farmer only learns the result at delivery, with nothing to check. (~15 s)

The problem

And that count decides how much the farmer is paid

~550 €

per tonne: the difference between lentils sold for people to eat and seeds sold as animal feed

Up to 5-8 M€

of damaged lentils removed and lost in 2025, a cost that lands on farmers (our estimate, a maximum)

38,000 t

more lentils imported than exported by France in 2024/25, mostly from Canada

Sources: FranceAgriMer producer prices (806-873 €/t); CRIT Grand Est 2025 (feed 200-260 €/t); Terres Univia trade data. 5-8 M€ = 24.4 % × estimated harvest × ~556 €/t.

And the count decides the price: about 550 euros a tonne between food and feed. In 2025, up to 5 to 8 million euros of damaged lentils were sorted out and lost, our estimate and a maximum. France still imports 38,000 tonnes more lentils than it exports. (~15 s)

How it helps

How a better count changes things

Seeds get damaged

a little in some trucks, a lot in others

The damage sets the price

damaged seeds are removed and lost

But it’s counted by eye

slow, uneven, and nobody can check it

SoyMate

the same photo count, for the farmer and the cooperative

The farmer

knows the result before delivering: can clean the seeds first, choose who to sell to, or show a photo if they disagree

The cooperative

knows right away where each truck should go, and every site counts the same way

Both

fewer arguments: one method, one photo per truck

We don’t stop the beetle. We make the count fast, the same everywhere, and visible to both sides.

So: damage sets the price, and it's counted by eye, slowly and unevenly, with no way to check. SoyMate doesn't stop the beetle. It gives the farmer and the cooperative the same count from a photo: the farmer knows before delivering and can clean first or pick a buyer; the cooperative routes each truck at once, the same way at every site. (~25 s)

Why soybean first

Soy is where we can build it today. Lentils are where the money is.

SoybeanLentil
Public photos of damaged seedsyes, about 8,000none found
Eaten by people in France45,000 t a year (tofu, soy drinks)almost the whole harvest
Quality problem in 20251 lot in 3 had too many unripe seeds1 seed in 4 damaged (average truckload)
Extra value when sold to eat, not as feed20 to 70 € per tonne~550 € per tonne

So we use soy to build and test the method, then bring it to lentils, where getting the count right is worth 8 to 25 times more per tonne.

Sources: Mendeley datasets d97rjyk2tz and v6vzvfszj6; FranceAgriMer oilseed sheet 2026 (45 kt); Terres Inovia soy and lentil quality sheets 2025; Terres Univia price observatory (soy gap “très faible”), Terres Inovia 2024 (~70 €/t).

Why soybean? It is the only bean with public photos of damaged seeds, about 8,000; for lentils we found none. Food soy is real in France but pays little extra; lentils pay about 550 euros more per tonne. So we build and test on soy, and take it to lentils. (~15 s)

What we built

Take a photo, get a grade, and see how sure it is

1

Photo

one phone photo: seeds spread on a tray, or packed

2

Find

every seed is outlined, touching ones too

3

Check

each seed: sound, broken, stained, unripe, hole, or foreign material

4

Answer

share of each with its range: pass, not sure yet (add seeds), or fail

A packed lot it never saw: 77 objects found (the dataset's outlines: 80 seeds, 2 pieces of debris). 6.5 % defects, range 2.8 to 14.3 %: at a 5 % limit, "not sure yet".

Seeds found by colour segmentation (spread) or FastSAM (packed, experimental); each seed classified on frozen DINOv2 features. A few seconds per photo on a CPU.

One photo of the sample. The app outlines every seed, checks each one, and gives the share of each defect with its range. If the range straddles the limit, it says not sure yet and asks for more seeds instead of guessing. Here, a packed lot it never saw in training. (~15 s)

Live demo

Real photos, graded live

1. Many seeds

a farmer's photo: all 164 seeds found, 18 broken (11 %), so it fails a 5 % limit

2. One seed

a single seed with a defect: insect hole, 100 % sure, the same as the dataset's label

Try it live: 18.206.176.19, on any phone or laptop, examples included

The recording plays on its own while this slide is up; it is the same app, live at 18.206.176.19. First a farmer's photo from Ghana: 164 seeds on paper, a photo it never trained on. It finds all 164, the same as the published hand count, and checks each one: 18 are broken, 11 %, with a range of 7.1 to 16.7 %. At a 5 % limit that is a clear fail. Then a single seed: it names the defect, an insect hole, the exit hole of a storage beetle, 100 % sure and matching the dataset's label. One seed alone can't pass or fail a lot, so it tells you to photograph a handful. If you demo live and it fails, come back to this slide: the recording shows the same thing. (~45 s)

Is it a solution?

To work for French lentils, four things must happen

1

Photos of French lentils

checked by expert graders. In our tests, 50 local seeds per type scored 0.93; 1,000 from another dataset scored 0.52

2

Enough seeds per truck

about 1,000 seeds (a few photos), so the result is within 3 points

3

Tested against expert counts

the way grain inspectors test any machine before they trust it

4

A trial with one cooperative

to check it really changes decisions: fewer disputes, trucks sent to the right place

Sources: our transfer test between two soybean datasets (R3, sound vs broken, macro F1); USDA grain inspection notice PN-26-03; binomial ranges at lentil damage levels.

For French lentils, four things must happen. Lentil photos checked by experts: our tests say local labels matter far more than borrowed ones, 50 seeds per type from the new setup beat 1,000 from another dataset. Enough seeds per truck. Testing against expert counts. And a trial with one cooperative. Each is measurable: a clear yes or no. (~20 s)

Why it can last

There is room to make money

People already pay for it

in Australia, grain buyers use a company (Cropify) that grades lentils with AI

Nobody does it in France

the French leader (Inarix) only grades cereals like wheat and barley

Every tonne counts

lentils sold to eat are worth ~550 € more per tonne than animal feed

Easy to roll out

just a phone: no machine to buy or install

Sources: ChannelLife 20/8/2026 and Stock Journal 4/9/2026 (Cropify; judged worth “commercial consideration” by Grain Trade Australia); Meta AI blog 6/12/2024 and inarix.com.

Buyers already pay for AI lentil grading in Australia. Nobody does it in France, where the leader grades cereals only. Ours needs just a phone. (~10 s)

Next step

One cooperative,
one lentil harvest

A pilot that measures whether a grade both sides can check changes decisions and protects farmer income.
